findings.verdict: mitigated by a custom escaper; hardening recommended
findings.rationale: Each flagged innerHTML assignment interpolates server-provided text only through esc() at the point of insertion (message text, artifact names, activity text via esc(text) at line 156, proposal head/main/note via esc() at line 144, sponsor and event fields in the proof dialog). Values inserted without esc() are numbers from money()/counts, fixed enum class names, or nested fragments whose own text is escaped. Snyk cannot recognise a project-local sanitizer, so the alert is expected.
findings.recommendation: Owner ROOT/DEMO, optional hardening before freeze: add a unit test that renders a message, artifact name, note and event detail containing and asserts the DOM contains no element from it; or build these regions with document.createElement/textContent instead of template strings. Do not add a Snyk ignore without that test.

findings.rationale: The server is loopback-only: main.ts listens on 127.0.0.1 and every request is rejected unless the Host header is localhost or 127.0.0.1; no network transmission leaves the machine. TLS on loopback would add no protection for the judge run.
findings.recommendation: Owner JUDGES: state this explicitly in docs/SECURITY.md (already implied by the threat model). No code change.

findings.verdict: accepted by design, minor tightening possible
findings.rationale: The catch handler returns error.message only for StateError instances, whose messages are the deliberate user-facing texts; every other error is replaced by a fixed sentence. The proposed RocketRide hook and some 503 paths embed a truncated provider/error message inside a StateError, which is the only channel where third-party text could reach the client.
findings.recommendation: Owner ROOT, optional: for StateError with status >= 500 return a fixed sentence and keep the detailed text in the conversation event/receipt only.
